title: Global power-lifting test for adequate affineness over an affine base
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A$ be a commutative $k$-algebra, and let $f:\mathcal U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism from an algebraic stack over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $f$ is adequately affine [def-sfb-adequately-affine-morphism] if and only if, for every surjection $\mathcal B\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$-algebras and every $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal U,\mathcal C)$, there exist $N>0$ and $s\in\Gamma(\mathcal U,\mathcal B)$ with image $t^N$. Quasi-coherent algebras, surjections and global sections use [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. This criterion does not require $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal U,\mathcal O)$ to be an isomorphism and imposes no Noetherian or finite-generation hypothesis.

source.place: Remark 4.1.3 and Lemma 4.1.8(2),(3), printed pp.17--20. This node states only the equivalence with adequate affineness, not the adequate-moduli conclusion of Remark 5.1.2. Primary arXiv:1005.2398v3 read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Assume $f$ adequately affine. Fix a surjection $\mathcal B\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C$ on $\mathcal U$ and $t\in\Gamma(\mathcal U,\mathcal C)$. The identity smooth test $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ in [def-sfb-adequately-affine-morphism] gives an etale cover of $Y$ on which positive powers of $t$ lift to the direct image of $\mathcal B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-sieve-finite-affine-refinement] to the covering sieve generated by that cover on the final object of $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$. We obtain finitely many affine etale $W_j=\operatorname{Spec}A_j\to Y$, jointly surjective, each factoring through a cover member. Restrict its local lift to $W_j$: there are $n_j>0$ and $b_j\in\Gamma(\mathcal U_{W_j},\mathcal B_{W_j})$ mapping to $t_{W_j}^{n_j}$. These are precisely the sections in the direct-image formula. The stacks $\mathcal U_{W_j}$ are algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products].

source.place: Remark 4.1.3, Lemma 4.1.8(2),(3), and the faithfully flat descent argument of Lemmas 3.1.3 and 3.4.4; read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3. Local PDF WANTED; argument expanded by NW using the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: If $Y$ is empty, then $\mathcal U$ is empty and both section rings are zero; $N=1,s=0$ works. Otherwise the finite covering family is nonempty. Put $S=\prod_j A_j$ and $N=\prod_j n_j>0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}S=\coprod_j W_j$, with the stated component maps. Each $A_j$ is flat over $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Hence $S$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-product-flat-modules], and faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat], since the component maps jointly cover $Y$. Raise $b_j$ to $N/n_j$, giving a lift of $t^N$ on each component. The disjoint open cover of $\mathcal U_S$ by $\mathcal U_{W_j}$ has empty pairwise intersections. Thus these sections agree on intersections and glue by the sheaf axiom to $b_S\in\Gamma(\mathcal U_S,\mathcal B_S)$ mapping to $t_S^N$.

source.place: Remark 4.1.3, Lemma 4.1.8(2),(3), and the faithfully flat descent argument of Lemmas 3.1.3 and 3.4.4; read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3. Local PDF WANTED; argument expanded by NW using the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: Let $M=\Gamma(\mathcal U,\mathcal B)$, $L=\Gamma(\mathcal U,\mathcal C)$, and $h:M\to L$ be the induced $A$-linear map. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-stack-flat-scalar-sections] hold: $f$ is qcqs and $A\to S$ is flat. Its natural algebra isomorphisms identify $b_S$ with an element of $M\otimes_A S$ whose image under $h\otimes1$ is $t^N\otimes1$. Form the $A$-module $K=L/\operatorname{im}h$. The sequence $M\to L\to K\to0$ is exact by the definition of the quotient. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], the class of $t^N\otimes1$ vanishes in $K\otimes_A S$. The injectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] therefore implies $[t^N]=0$ in $K$. Consequently $t^N=h(s)$ for some $s\in M$. This proves the global power-lifting condition.

source.place: Remark 4.1.3, Lemma 4.1.8(2),(3), and the faithfully flat descent argument of Lemmas 3.1.3 and 3.4.4; read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3. Local PDF WANTED; argument expanded by NW using the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: Conversely assume global power lifting on $\mathcal U$. Fix any smooth test $T\to Y$, a section $t\in(f_*\mathcal C)(T)$, and an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq T$. The test stack $\mathcal U_V=\mathcal U\times_Y V$ is algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. Its projection $q:\mathcal U_V\to\mathcal U$ is affine by [lem-sfb-stack-affine-algebra-direct-image], applied to $A\to R$. In fact, take any surjection $\mathcal D\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal E$ of quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal U_V$ and any section $u\in\Gamma(\mathcal U_V,\mathcal E)$. The same node gives a surjection $q_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal D\twoheadrightarrow q_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal E$ on $\mathcal U$ and natural global-section ring isomorphisms. Under these isomorphisms $u$ is a target section on $\mathcal U$. The assumed property produces a lift of $u^m$ for some $m>0$; the natural ring isomorphisms transfer this lift back to $\Gamma(\mathcal U_V,\mathcal D)$. Thus every algebra surjection on this test stack has global power lifting, whether or not it is a pullback from $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Remark 4.1.3, Lemma 4.1.8(2),(3), and the faithfully flat descent argument of Lemmas 3.1.3 and 3.4.4; read online at https://arxiv.org/html/1005.2398v3. Local PDF WANTED; argument expanded by NW using the cited DAG statements.

proof.text: For the particular surjection $\mathcal B\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal C$ of the definition, restriction to $\mathcal U_V$ is still a surjection of quasi-coherent algebras. Indeed, restriction in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] is precomposition: a local lift on an object over a scheme $Z$ remains a lift after an fppf cover of $Z$, whose maps to $V$ are obtained by composition. The same observation restricts a local free presentation of the underlying module; the structure sheaf has the same value on that object. Hence the restricted modules remain quasi-coherent. Step 4, with $u=t|_V$ and this restricted surjection, gives a lift of a positive power of $t|_V$. The affine opens $V$ cover $T$ and are etale over $T$. The displayed direct-image formula in [def-sfb-adequately-affine-morphism] therefore makes these lifts precisely the required etale-local power lifts on every smooth test. With the given qcqs hypothesis, this is adequate affineness of $f$. No structural-ring isomorphism, Noetherian assumption, or finite-generation restriction was used.
